name: Learn pet first aid
blurb: What to do in the minutes before the vet, and just as importantly what not to do — several common human remedies are toxic to pets.
gear: Your vet and nearest emergency vet numbers saved
steps: Save your vet and out-of-hours emergency vet numbers in your phone now, and know the route.
Learn normal vital signs for your animal so you can recognise abnormal ones.
Learn to control bleeding with direct pressure, and how to muzzle safely — a frightened animal in pain may bite the person helping it.
Learn the common emergencies: bloat in deep-chested dogs, heatstroke, seizures, and blocked bladders in male cats. All are time-critical.
Learn the toxic list: chocolate, xylitol, grapes and raisins, lilies for cats, ibuprofen and paracetamol. Never give human painkillers.
Learn safe transport for an injured animal and when moving them is the wrong call.
tips: Never induce vomiting unless a vet tells you to. With some substances it causes far worse damage.
Paracetamol is lethal to cats in small doses. Keep all human medication well away from pets.
proof: A course certificate, an assembled kit, and emergency numbers everyone in the house can find.
